heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷上 睦親 15 · 教子當在幼 … 同居相處貴愛

items.text: Treat all your children equally in food, clothing, and affection, and teach them early to distinguish elder from younger and right from wrong.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 飲食、衣服之愛不可不均一 — Love in food and clothing must be equal.

items.text: Yield to your younger brother rather than contend, especially if your parents show him more love.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 長者宜少讓 — The elder should yield a little.

items.text: Restrain yourself and do not presume on your parents' favor to act arrogantly toward your elder brother.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 幼者宜自抑 — The younger should restrain himself.

items.text: If your father favors a stepmother or a favored concubine over you, obey him wholeheartedly; in time your sincerity will set things right.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 為子者要當一意承順 — As a son, you must obey with single-minded compliance.

items.text: Even if your parents-in-law favor your sister-in-law, serve them with single-minded obedience; in time they will come to their senses.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 為兒婦者要當一意承順 — As a daughter-in-law, you must obey with single-minded compliance.

items.text: When sharing anything from the common store, be scrupulously fair; do not secretly take more, even if the item is worth only a few cash.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 眾有所分，雖果實之屬，直不數十文，亦必均平 — When distributing anything, even fruit worth not a few dozen cash, it must be even.

items.text: Do not use your seniority to oppress your younger brothers or to monopolize common wealth for your own comfort; keep accounts open and let them share in management.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 專用其財，自取溫飽，因而成私 — He takes the common wealth for his own comfort and turns it private.

items.text: Respect your elder brother's oversight; listen to his counsel and do not steal or misuse the common property.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 幼必長聽 — The younger must listen to the elder.

items.text: If you are richer, share your surplus with your poorer brother without expecting gratitude; if poorer, accept your lot and do not envy or demand.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 富者時分惠其餘，不恤其不知恩；貧者知自有定分，不望其必分惠 — The rich should share surplus without caring if they are ungrateful; the poor should know their own lot and not expect gifts.

items.text: Do not hoard private gold and silver; use it to buy productive land or lend it to the common household so that brothers and nephews all benefit.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 將私財假於眾，使之營家而止取其本者 — Lend private wealth to the common household to run the family and take only the principal.

items.text: When living in a common gate with separate households, each must take care of shared courtyards and not let your children or servants disturb or litter the common areas.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 於眾事宜各盡心，不可令小兒、婢僕有擾於眾 — In shared matters, each must do his best; do not let children or servants disturb the common.

items.text: When a household member is unreasonable and constantly annoys you, keep a generous heart and endure it patiently as a matter of necessity.
items.citation: Yuanshi Shifan, Juan Shang Mu Qin 15
items.quote: 當寬其懷抱，以無可奈何處之 — Keep a broad heart and deal with it as unavoidable.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷中 處己 12 · 人不可懷慢偽妒疑之心 … 浮言不足恤

items.text: Instruct and reprove your child when he does wrong, for no one else will do it.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 12
items.quote: 人有過失，非其父兄，孰肯誨責 — When a person has faults, who but his father and elder brothers is willing to instruct and reprove him?

items.text: Instruct and reprove your younger sibling when he does wrong, for no one else will do it.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 12
items.quote: 人有過失，非其父兄，孰肯誨責 — When a person has faults, who but his father and elder brothers is willing to instruct and reprove him?

items.text: If a wayward young relative does not change despite reproof, accept it as hopeless and do not keep nagging, lest you increase resentment.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 12
items.quote: 雖其至親，亦當處之無可奈何，不必譊譊 — Even his closest kin should accept it as hopeless and not keep nagging.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷下 治家 71 · 造橋修路宜助財力 … 起造宜以漸經營

items.text: In all buying and selling, be honest and do not adulterate goods, so your household will not be ruined by loss and divine retribution, and you can support your wife and children.
items.quote: 凡物貨必真，又須敬惜 — All goods must be genuine, and must be handled with reverence and care.

items.text: Plan and build your house gradually over many years, not all at once, so that your household remains wealthy and is not forced to borrow or sell property.
items.quote: 以漸為之，則屋成而家富自若 — Do it gradually; then the house is finished and the household remains well-off.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷中 處己 50 · 子弟當謹交遊 … 訟不可長

items.text: Regulate their going out and coming in and be careful about their friends; do not shut them up at home.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 50
items.quote: 時其出入，謹其交遊 — regulate their going out and coming in and be careful about their friends.

items.text: Each of you sons and younger brothers should economize and limit your expenses, lest you ruin the family fortune.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 50
items.quote: 為子弟者各宜量節 — sons and younger brothers should each economize.

items.text: Remember how your father and grandfather built up the family, and continue their sacrifices.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 50
items.quote: 思與之延其祭祀 — think of continuing their sacrifices.
items.conflict: Ancestral sacrifices are idolatry; worship God alone (Exod 20:3-5).

items.text: Do not treat your children as strangers; provide for them so they are not left to hunger and cold.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 50
items.quote: 多生男女，視如路人 — having many sons and daughters, treat them like strangers.

items.text: Plan ahead: provide him a livelihood and teach him a trade.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 50
items.quote: 有男而為之營生，教之生業 — if you have a son, arrange a livelihood for him and teach him a trade.

items.text: Save early for her clothes and dowry, so that when you send her off to marry it costs no effort.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 50
items.quote: 養女，亦當早為儲蓄衣衾、妝奩之具 — if you have a daughter, you should early save up clothes and trousseau items.

items.text: Prepare the graveclothes, coffin, and burial plot for the old people of the house early, so that when the time comes you need not sell fields or houses.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 50
items.quote: 家有老人，而送終之具不為素辦 — if there are old people in the family, and the things for their funerals are not prepared in advance.

items.text: Choose a means of livelihood so that you can serve your parents above and raise your children below.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 50
items.quote: 欲為仰事俯育之計 — if you want to make provision for serving those above and nourishing those below.

items.text: Run the household with order and discipline, as if it were a public office.
items.citation: 袁氏世範, 卷中 處己 50
items.quote: 居家當如居官，必有綱紀 — when at home, behave as if in office and have discipline.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷中 處己 31 · 諛巽之言多奸詐 … 人為情惑則忘返

items.text: Do not tell all private matters even to close relatives, lest later estrangement give them material for dispute against you.
items.quote: 親戚故舊，人情厚密之時，不可盡以密私之事語之 — When relations are close, do not tell all private matters to relatives and old friends.

items.text: When angry with a relative, do not expose his hidden shame or his father's or grandfather's faults; such words wound deeper than spears.
items.quote: 大抵忿怒之際，最不可指其隱諱之事，而暴其父祖之惡 — When angry, never point out his hidden shame or expose his father's or grandfather's faults.

items.text: Even when reproving a relative's fault, keep a warm face and humble tone, so that even if he does not heed, he will not be angered.
items.quote: 且如諫人之短，語雖切直，而能溫顏下氣，縱不見聽，亦未必怒 — When reproving one's fault, though the words be direct, with a warm face and humble manner, even if not heeded, he will not be angry.

items.text: Do not dress or ride in gaudy style in your home region, lest your poor relatives and old friends feel ashamed and keep away from you.
items.quote: 居於鄉曲，輿馬衣服不可鮮花。蓋鄉曲親故，居貧者多 — In your home region, do not have gaudy carriages and clothes; for relatives there are mostly poor.

items.text: Do not give yourself to lust and ruin your household; it begins with a first try, and without discernment you cannot turn back.
items.quote: 子弟有耽於情欲，迷而忘返，至於破家而不悔者，蓋始於試為之 — A young son who indulges lust, lost beyond return, ruins his family without regret; it begins with trying.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷上 睦親 62 · 分給財產務均平 … 人行有長短

items.text: Divide property equally among your descendants without partiality, so that no dispute arises.
items.quote: 父、祖出於公心，初無偏曲 — Father and grandfather act with public-minded fairness, without initial partiality.

items.text: If one of your descendants is dissolute, give him only grain and goods, not land, lest he sell it and harm the other branches.
items.quote: 止可逐時均給財穀，不可均給田產 — Only distribute goods and grain at the time, not land.

items.text: Make your will fairly; do not let a fierce wife or a cunning concubine cause you to favor some sons over others.
items.quote: 亦須公平，乃可以保家 — It must be fair, then it can preserve the family.

items.text: While you are in health, write your will; do not delay until sickness makes you unable to speak or move.
items.quote: 常欲預為遺囑之文，而不知風燭不常 — Often wish to make a will, but know not that wind-blown candle is not constant.

items.text: Use family fields to endow schools and monasteries: train the able as scholars and make monks of the rest, so no one is left destitute or disgraces his ancestors.
items.quote: 不若以其田置義學及依寺院置度僧出 — Better to use the fields for charity schools and for ordaining monks at temples.
items.conflict: Monastic vows are unbiblical; provide for the needy through work and charity, not by making them monks.

items.text: Do not scheme to let your children enjoy wealth from childhood without hardship; your human plans cannot overcome heaven.
items.quote: 欲其子孫自少小安然享大富貴，尤其蔽惑也 — Wanting their descendants from childhood to enjoy great wealth at ease is especially deluded.

items.text: If you sit in comfort because of your father's or grandfather's wealth or office, do not become proud and thus shame yourself.
items.quote: 因父祖之遺資而坐享肥濃 — Because of father's or grandfather's inheritance, sit enjoying richness.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷中 處己 66 · 暴吏害民必天誅 … 小兒不可獨遊街市

items.text: Keep the walls high and thick, fences dense, doors and windows strong; repair them promptly and fit grates over water channels, so that thieves cannot break in and servants or idle sons cannot slip out at night.
items.quote: 垣牆高厚，藩籬周密，窗壁門關堅牢...免奴婢奔竄及不肖子弟夜出之患 — Make walls high and thick, fences dense, doors strong; so servants cannot flee and idle sons cannot slip out at night.

items.text: Take turns with the servants to patrol the interior of the house at night, as the head of the house directs.
items.quote: 若屋之內，則子弟及奴婢更迭巡警 — Inside the house, the sons and servants take turns on watch.

items.text: In a secluded valley or village, build lodges at key points and invite strong households to live there, so that in fire or theft they can come to one another's aid.
items.quote: 居止或在山谷村野僻靜之地，須于周圍要害去處置立莊屋，招誘丁多之人居之。或有火燭、竊盜，可以即相救應。 — In a secluded place, build lodges at key points and invite strong men to live there, so that in fire or theft they may help one another.

items.text: If you hear a thief at night, call out plainly and rise slowly to drive him off; do not strike in the dark, lest the thief wound you or you hit your own family.
items.quote: 夜間覺有盜，便須直言「有盜」，徐起逐之...不可乘暗擊之...及誤擊自家之人 — If you hear a thief at night, call out plainly and rise slowly; do not strike in the dark, lest you hit your own people.

items.text: Set watchers at the roads, prepare a side door for old, young, and women to flee, and have sons and servants keep weapons ready; resist if you can, flee if not, but never let the bandits seize a family member as hostage.
items.quote: 仍預置便門，遇有警急，老幼婦女且從便門走避。又須子弟及僕者平時常備器械，為禦敵之計。可敵則敵，不可敵則避，切不可令盜得我之人，執以為質 — Prepare a side door for old, young, and women to flee; have sons and servants keep weapons ready; resist if you can, flee if not, but never let the bandits take a hostage.

items.text: If something is lost, search quickly, but do not rashly suspect anyone in the house; by suspicion you may wrong an innocent person and make the thief bold.
items.quote: 家居或有失物，不可不急尋。急尋，則人或投之僻處...又不可妄猜疑人...況疑心一生，則所疑之人揣其行坐辭色皆若竊物，而實未嘗有所竊也 — If something is lost, search quickly, but do not rashly suspect anyone; suspicion makes the innocent seem guilty.

items.text: Show kindness and favor to your neighbors so that in a fire they will come to your aid; do not oppress them with official power.
items.quote: 居宅不可無鄰家...又須平時撫恤鄰里有恩義。有士大夫平時多以官勢殘虐鄰里...鄰里甘受杖而坐視其大廈為煨燼 — A house must have neighbors; be kind and helpful to them, not oppressive, so that in a fire they will help.

items.text: Take every precaution against fire: keep the kitchen swept, watch that bedding does not cover embers, guard silkworm sheds, manure heaps, dead ashes, thatched roofs, high wind, oil and lime.
items.quote: 火之所起，多從廚灶...烘焙物色過夜...積油物、積石灰須常防火 — Fire often starts from the stove; be careful with embers, oil, and lime.

items.text: Do not deck a small child with gold, silver, or jewels, lest a greedy man kill him in a lonely place for the ornaments.
items.quote: 富人有愛其小兒者，以金銀寶珠之屬飾其身。小人有貪者，於僻靜處壞其性命而取其物 — Do not deck a child with gold and jewels, lest a greedy man kill him for them.

items.text: In a town or market, do not let a small child wander the streets unless a strong man carries or leads him, for fear of kidnappers.
items.quote: 市邑小兒，非有壯夫攜負，不可令遊街巷，慮有誘略之人也 — In towns, a child must not go on the streets unless a strong man carries or leads him, for fear of kidnappers.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷下 治家 55 · 田產界至宜分明 … 賦稅早納為上

items.text: When dividing the family estate, carefully fix and record the boundaries of fields, gardens, and hill land, so that no dispute arises.
items.quote: 人有田園山地，界至不可不分明。異居分析之初，置產、典買之際，尤不可不仔細。

items.text: When drawing up the inheritance lots, record every share so that each heir sees all shares, and append any special grants, so that nothing is concealed and no one may later demand a redivision.
items.quote: 若互見他分，厚薄肥瘠可以畢見...並宜於鬮書後開具...不在開具之數則為漏鬮，雖分析後，許應分人別求均分。

items.text: When you divide the household, have the allotment document officially stamped without delay, to cut off future disputes.
items.quote: 凡析戶之家宜即印鬮書，以杜後患。

items.text: Do not assign all your property to one heir's name to evade corvée, for your descendants will then fight over it.
items.quote: 人有求避役者...令一人認役...而其子孫有欲執書契而掩有之者，遂興訴訟。

items.text: Do not falsely register under a kinsman's official household to escape corvée, for it sows future lawsuits.
items.quote: 人有已分財產而欲避免差役，則冒同宗有官之人為一戶籍者，皆他日爭訟之端由也。

items.text: Set aside the tax funds first, then use the remainder for daily expenses; do not touch the tax reserve, or you will ruin the household.
items.quote: 凡有家產，必有稅賦，須是先截留輸納之資，卻將贏餘分給日用...不可侵支輸納之資...是皆可以耗家。

items.text: When buying property from a relative, offer a fair price and do not exploit the relationship to beat it down.
items.quote: 凡鄰近利害欲得之產，宜稍增其價，不可恃其有親有鄰及以典至買及無人敢買而扼損其價。

items.text: Do not buy property with legal defects to save money, for you will leave lawsuits to your descendants.
items.quote: 凡田產有交關違條者，雖其價廉，不可與之交易...自遺患與患及子孫者甚多。

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷下 治家 17 · 小兒不可臨深 … 凡物各宜得所

items.text: Guard your children from danger: fence wells and ponds, and keep them away from steep places and dangerous objects.
items.quote: 不可令小兒狎而臨之 — Do not let children play near them.

items.text: When entertaining relatives and guests, do not force them to drink excessively; ensure they get home safely.
items.quote: 親賓相訪，不可多虐以酒 — When relatives and guests visit, do not abuse them with too much wine.

items.text: Enforce the separation of inner and outer quarters: allow no servant to enter the inner gate without urgent need, and no woman of the household to leave without cause.
items.quote: 令僕子非有警急修葺，不得入中門；婦女婢妾無故不得出中門。 — Order that male servants, except for urgent repairs, may not enter the inner gate; women and maids may not go out without reason.

items.text: Keep proper distance from maidservants and concubines; do not allow intimacy that leads to suspicion and disorder.
items.quote: 婢妾與主翁親近，或多挾此私通 — If maidservants and concubines become intimate with the master, many will use this for illicit relations.
items.conflict: Concubinage and extramarital intimacy are contrary to Scripture (Genesis 2:24, 1 Corinthians 7:2).

items.text: Do not rely on hired guardians to watch over concubines or paramours outside the main house; they may be bribed and your own child may be substituted.
items.quote: 所委監守之人得其犒遺，反與外人為耳目以通往來 — The guards you entrust may receive bribes and become spies for outsiders.
items.conflict: Concubinage and substitute children are contrary to God's order for family (Malachi 2:15).

items.text: Teach the women of the household to treat maidservants with patience, not with harshness and cruelty.
items.quote: 婦人既多褊急狠愎，暴忍殘刻，又不知古今道理 — Women are often narrow-minded, harsh, and cruel, and do not know reason.

items.text: Teach your children to value their own virtue and learning, not to desire clever and cunning servants.
items.quote: 不求自己德業之出眾。而獨欲僕者峭黠之出眾。 — They do not seek to excel in virtue and learning, but only desire servants who are clever and cunning.

items.text: Provide your servants with adequate clothing and food; do not let them suffer cold or hunger.
items.quote: 衣須令其溫，食須令其飽 — Their clothing must keep them warm, their food must fill them.

items.text: In winter, make sure your servants' sleeping quarters are sheltered from wind and cold.
items.quote: 令冬時無風寒之患 — Let them have no suffering from wind and cold in winter.

items.text: Deal with servants justly: dismiss the incorrigible without violence; turn over criminals to the magistrate; for minor faults, be lenient.
items.quote: 婢僕有頑很全不中使令者，宜善遣之 — If a servant is stubborn and utterly unfit for command, you should dismiss him kindly.

items.text: When punishing servants for minor faults, do not strike them yourself in anger; have another carry out the punishment after calm deliberation.
items.quote: 婢僕有小過，不可親自鞭撻 — For small faults, do not personally whip servants.

items.text: After punishing a servant, do not hold a grudge; treat them as before, lest they despair and harm themselves.
items.quote: 婢僕有過，既以鞭撻，而呼喚使令，辭色如常 — After whipping a servant for a fault, when calling and commanding him, let your words and manner be as usual.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷上 睦親 45 · 立嗣擇昭穆相順 … 收養親戚當慮後患

items.text: Bring up the kinsman you adopt as your own son and give him your property.
items.quote: 惟當撫之如子，以其財產與之 — Treat him as a son and give him your property.

items.text: Serve the one who adopted you as your own father.
items.quote: 受所養者奉所養如父 — The one adopted serves the adopter as a father.

items.text: Continue the family sacrifices as the appointed heir.
items.quote: 以奉祭祀 — to serve the sacrifices
items.conflict: biblical prohibition of worshiping the dead (Deut 18:10-12)

items.text: Take in and educate your children born outside or after your death promptly, settling their status while you live.
items.quote: 別宅子、遺腹子宜及早收養教訓 — Children born of a separate house or posthumous should be taken in and taught early.

items.text: Decide early whether to raise a stepchild from your spouse's former marriage, and settle it before all to avoid dispute.
items.quote: 娶妻而有前夫之子，接腳夫而有前妻之子，欲撫養不欲撫養，尤不可不早定 — If you marry a woman with a son by her former husband, or a man with a son by his former wife, decide early whether to raise him.

items.text: Give an orphan girl a generous dowry and her due share of property.
items.quote: 孤女有分，必隨力厚嫁；合得田產，必依條分給 — An orphan girl has a share; give her a generous dowry and her due fields and property.

items.text: Arrange for an orphaned girl whose mother remarries to be raised in her paternal grandparents' home until marriage, to avoid suspicion.
items.quote: 如內外親戚有高義者，寧若與之議親，使鞠養于舅姑之家，俟其長而成親 — If a virtuous relative can arrange her betrothal, let her be raised in her husband's parents' home until she is grown and married.

items.text: Be mindful of your wife's helplessness and do not squander the family property.
items.quote: 苟為夫能念其妻之可憐 — If the husband can think of his wife's pitiable state.

items.text: Be mindful of your mother's helplessness and do not squander the family property.
items.quote: 為子能念其母之可憐 — If the son can think of his mother's pitiable state.

items.text: Do not betroth your children while they are still young; wait to see their character and circumstances.
items.quote: 人之男女，不可于幼小之時便議婚姻 — Children should not be betrothed while still young.

items.text: In arranging marriage, do not covet high rank or great wealth; seek a match equal in character.
items.quote: 男女議親，不可貪其閥閱之高，資產之厚 — In betrothing sons and daughters, do not covet high rank and great wealth.

items.text: Take in and support an elderly kinswoman whose own children are unfilial, and publicly certify she has no property to avoid trouble.
items.quote: 年老而子孫不肖，不能供養者，不可不收養 — if elderly and their children are unfilial and cannot support them, you must take them in.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷下 治家 39 · 人物之性皆貪生 … 鄰里貴和同

items.text: Nurse your own child yourself rather than giving him over to a wet nurse, lest the wet nurse's own child starve or her family be broken apart.
items.quote: 有子而不自乳，使他人乳之，前輩已言其非矣。 — If you have a child and do not nurse him yourself but give him to another to nurse, the ancients already said this is wrong.

items.text: When you take a man's wife or daughter as a servant, return her to her husband or parents at the end of her term; do not sell her to another or keep her for life.
items.quote: 以人之妻為婢，年滿而送還其夫；以人之女為婢，年滿而送還其父母。 — Take a man's wife as a servant, and when her term is up send her back to her husband; take a man's daughter as a servant, and when her term is up send her back to her parents.

items.text: If a servant has no family to rely on, remembering her labor you must not fail to support her; arrange a marriage for her to prevent future trouble.
items.quote: 或有婢妾無夫、子、兄、弟可依，僕隸無家可歸，念其有勞不可不養者，當令預經鄰保，自言並陳於官。或預與之擇其配，婢使之嫁，僕使之娶。 — If a maid or concubine has no husband, children, or brothers to rely on, and a servant has no home to return to, remembering their work you must not fail to support them; have them report to the neighborhood and officials, and arrange marriages for them.

items.text: After buying a maid or servant, carefully ask where she came from; if she is a free person's child who was abducted, report to officials and do not return her to the trafficker.
items.quote: 買婢妾既已成契，不可不細詢其所自來。恐有良人子女，為人所誘略。果然，則即告之官，不可以婢妾還與引來之人。 — After buying a maid or concubine and making the contract, you must carefully ask where she came from; if she is a free person's child who was lured away, report it to the officials and do not give her back to the one who brought her.
items.conflict: Buying concubines or persons as property conflicts with Christian teaching on human dignity and monogamous marriage.

items.text: When buying a maid or servant, ask whether she may be sold; if not, do not make the contract. If she is truly destitute, have her report to officials and arrange for relatives to claim her.
items.quote: 買婢妾須問其應典賣不應典賣。如不應典賣則不可成契。或果窮乏無所倚依，須令經官自陳，下保審會，方可成契。 — When buying a maid or concubine, ask if she may be sold; if not, do not make the contract. If she is truly poor and has no support, have her report to the officials and get guarantors before making the contract.
items.conflict: Buying concubines or persons as property conflicts with Christian teaching on human dignity and monogamous marriage.

items.text: Do not employ cunning kinsmen or neighbors as your claws; instead, let your children associate with honest and upright people so that after you are gone they will be kept from ruin.
items.quote: 族人、鄰里、親戚有狡獪子弟，能恃強淩人...富家多用之以為爪牙...若平昔延接淳厚剛正之人，雖言語多拂人意，而子弟與之久處，則有身後之益。 — Among kinsmen, neighbors, and relatives there are cunning youths who bully others; rich families use them as claws... If you ordinarily welcome honest and upright people, though their words may offend, your children will benefit after you are gone.

items.text: When you entrust a manager with storerooms, money, or goods, keep a close eye on the accounts and choose trustworthy, cautious men, lest their hearts be tempted and they embezzle.
items.quote: 幹人有管庫者，須常謹其薄書，審其見存。幹人有貸財本興販者，須擇其淳厚，愛惜家累，方可付託。 — If a steward manages a storehouse, keep careful books and check the stock. If a steward handles money for trading, choose one who is honest and cares for his family before entrusting him.

items.text: Treat tenant farmers with generosity: help them at births, marriages, building, and deaths; reduce interest on loans; lower rent in bad years; make no unreasonable demands; love them as your own flesh.
items.quote: 遇其有生育、婚嫁、營造、死亡，當厚周之。耕耘之際，有所假貸，少收其息。水旱之年，察其所虧，早為除減。不可有非理之需...視之愛之，不啻如骨肉。 — When tenants have births, marriages, building, or deaths, help them generously; reduce interest on loans; in flood or drought years, lessen rent; do not make unreasonable demands... Love them as your own flesh.

items.text: Warn your household that tenant women or children who ask for loans or pledges secretly, saying 'do not let the master know,' intend to cheat; do not lend to them.
items.quote: 佃僕婦女等，有于人家婦女、小兒處稱「莫令家長知」，而欲重息以生借錢、穀...皆是有心脫漏，必無還意。為家長者宜常以此喻其家知也。 — Tenant women or children who say to your women or children, 'Don't let the master know,' and want to borrow money or grain at high interest are all cheats with no intention to repay. The master should warn his household about this.

items.text: Do not allow nuns, female religious, matchmakers, brokers, or women traders or healers into your home, lest they swindle your women or lead them into evil.
items.quote: 尼姑、道婆、媒婆、牙婆及婦人以買賣、針灸為名者，皆不可令入人家。凡脫漏婦女財物及引誘婦女為不美之事，皆此曹也。 — Nuns, Daoist women, matchmakers, brokers, and women who come under pretext of trade or healing must not be allowed into the house. Those who swindle women's goods or lead women into evil are all such persons.

items.text: In winter, when waters are low, lead in repairing ponds and dikes; when water is used, divide it fairly among neighboring families, and do not be stingy with food for laborers.
items.quote: 池塘、陂湖、河埭有眾享其溉田之利者，田多之家當相與率倡，令田主出食，佃人出力，遇冬時修築...及用水之際，遠近高下，分水必均。 — Where ponds and dikes benefit many, families with more land should lead; have the landowner provide food and tenants provide labor to repair them in winter; when using water, divide it equally regardless of distance or height.

items.text: Do not let a single root or shoot cause strife with your brother when dividing property; plant trees on waste land rather than quarrel over boundaries.
items.quote: 至於兄弟析產或因一根荄之微，忿爭失歡。比鄰山地偶有竹木在兩界之間，則興訟連年。 — When brothers divide property, over a single root or shoot they may get angry and lose harmony. Over bamboo or trees growing on a boundary between neighboring hills, they may litigate for years.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷上 睦親 31 · 友愛弟侄 … 養異姓子有礙

items.text: If your brother's child is orphaned, raise and educate him as your own child, so he is not left without support.
items.quote: 幼而無父母者，苟有伯叔父母，則不至無所養 — If a child loses his parents, if he has uncles and aunts, he will not lack for care.

items.text: Honor and support your uncles and aunts as you would your parents; if they are old and have no descendants, give them a home.
items.quote: 兄弟之子謂之猶子，亦謂其奉承報孝，有子之道 — A brother's son is called 'like a son'; he has the duty of serving and repaying as a son.

items.text: Model harmony with your own brothers and require your sons to serve their uncles well, so that they will be filial to you.
items.quote: 欲吾子之孝於己，須以其善事伯叔父者先之 — If you want your son to be filial to you, first have him serve his uncles well.

items.text: Do not pass on gossip or criticize others behind their backs, and do not eavesdrop; when approaching someone, make your presence known.
items.quote: 背後之言，人不傳遞，則彼不聞知，寧有忿爭？須揚聲曳履使人知之 — If backbiting words are not passed on, the other will not hear; how can there be resentment? When visiting, make your steps heard.

items.text: Do not stir up your husband with your words or let grievances against his relatives drive a wedge between him and his family.
items.quote: 婦女以言激怒其夫及同輩，輕於割恩，易於修怨 — Women use words to provoke their husbands and peers, quick to cut off affection, quick to nurse grudges.

items.text: If your brother is poor, relieve his need even if your wife opposes; be generous and do not covet his property.
items.quote: 外與兄弟相愛常不失歡，私救其所急，私周其所乏 — Outwardly love your brothers without losing harmony; secretly relieve their urgent needs and supply their wants.

items.text: When supporting your parents, do not insist that a poor sibling contribute equally; bear the greater cost rather than let your parents be neglected.
items.quote: 有不恤兄弟之貧，養親必欲如一，寧棄親而不顧者 — There are those who, not pitying a brother's poverty, insist on equal shares in supporting parents, even abandoning parents.

items.text: Do not assume your children are good; watch over their conduct and inquire diligently, for they may hide their faults.
items.quote: 子孫有過，多掩蔽父祖之耳目 — When descendants err, they often hide it from their fathers and grandfathers.

items.text: When a poor kinsman asks for help, give according to your means; do not lend and then demand repayment, which breeds resentment.
items.quote: 應親戚故舊有所假貸，不若隨力給與之 — When relatives ask to borrow, better to give according to your ability.

items.text: Choose an adopted child wisely: if you are poor, raise him from infancy with care; if rich, adopt when older so you can see his character.
items.quote: 貧者養他人之子當于幼時...富者養他人之子當於既長之時 — The poor should rear an adopted child from infancy; the rich should adopt him when already grown.

items.text: Serve your adoptive parents as your own parents, with filial devotion.
items.quote: 必能事所養為所生 — He will surely serve his adoptive parents as his own.

items.text: Do not adopt a child of another surname, for it troubles the ancestral spirits and risks forbidden same-surname marriage.
items.quote: 養異姓之子，非惟祖先神靈不歆其祀，數世之後，必與同姓通婚姻者 — Adopting a child of a different surname means the ancestral spirits will not accept his offerings, and after some generations he may marry someone of the same surname.
items.conflict: Ancestor veneration and clan purity; adoption should be based on love and providence, not ancestral concerns.

heading: 袁氏世範 Yuanshi Shifan · Yuan Cai · 袁氏世範 卷上 睦親 1 · 性不可以強合 … 子弟不可廢學

items.text: Understand your child's nature; do not force him to be exactly like you, but accommodate differences.
items.quote: 父必欲子之性合於己，子之性未必然；兄必欲弟之性合于己，弟之性未必然。 — A father always wants his son's nature to match his own, but it is not necessarily so; an elder brother always wants his younger brother's nature to match his own, but it is not necessarily so.

items.text: When you remonstrate with your parents, do so gently; if they do not accept, remain respectful and do not disobey; labor without resentment.
items.quote: 事父母，幾諫，見志不從，又敬不違，勞而不怨。 — In serving parents, remonstrate gently; if you see they are not inclined to follow, remain respectful and do not disobey; labor without complaining.

items.text: Reflect on your own youth as a son; if your own conduct toward your parents was imperfect, do not harshly blame your son.
items.quote: 吾今日為人之父，蓋前日嘗為人之子矣。倘吾前日事親之道有所未善，將以責其子，得不有愧於心！ — I am now a father, but formerly I was a son; if my own service to my parents was not perfect, would I not be ashamed to demand it of my son?

items.text: Be strict with your young son so he fears wrongdoing; but as he grows, do not withdraw your love.
items.quote: 父嚴而子知所畏，則不敢為非；父寬則子玩易，而恣其所行矣。 — If a father is strict, the son knows fear and dares not do wrong; if a father is lenient, the son becomes careless and does as he pleases.

items.text: Do not treat your parents as equals or argue about right and wrong; if they are wrong, remonstrate gently, and if they insist, accept it without disputing.
items.quote: 子之于父，弟之于兄，猶卒伍之於將帥，胥吏之于官曹，奴婢之于雇主，不可相視如朋輩，事事欲論曲直。 — A son to his father, a younger brother to his elder brother, are like soldiers to their general; they must not treat them as equals and argue about right and wrong.

items.text: Treat your elder brother as a superior, not an equal; if he is wrong, gently remonstrate; if he imposes something unreasonable, accept it obediently.
items.quote: 弟之于兄，猶卒伍之於將帥，不可相視如朋輩。 — A younger brother to his elder brother is like a soldier to his general; he must not treat him as an equal.

items.text: When a family member offends you, do not store up resentment; forgive immediately and excuse their faults.
items.quote: 人之犯我，藏蓄而不發，不過一再而已。積之既多，其發也，如洪流之決，不可遏矣。不若隨而解之，不置胸次。 — If someone offends me and I store it up without venting, it can only happen once or twice; when much is accumulated, its outburst is like a flood bursting, impossible to stop. It is better to resolve it immediately and not keep it in mind.

items.text: After a falling out, be the first to humble yourself and speak; do not let pride keep the rift open.
items.quote: 骨肉之失歡，有本於至微而終至不可解者。止由失歡之後，各自負氣，不肯先下爾。 — Estrangement among blood relatives often begins from something very small and ends up irresolvable, solely because after the falling out, each clings to his own pride and refuses to yield first.

items.text: When your husband is frustrated by poverty, be especially compliant and do not take offense at his harsh words.
items.quote: 破蕩之家，妻孥未嘗有過，而家長每多責駡者，衣食不給，觸事不諧，積忿無所發，惟可施于妻孥之前而已。妻孥能知此，則尤當奉承。 — In a declining household, wife and children may have done no wrong, but the head of the family often scolds them because food and clothing are lacking and nothing goes well; his accumulated anger has nowhere else to go but upon them. If wife and children understand this, they should be especially accommodating.

items.text: Humor the elderly: give them small gifts of food and money, let them play with children, and accommodate their childish ways.
items.quote: 年高之人，作事有如嬰孺，喜得錢財微利，喜受飲食、果食小惠，喜與孩童玩狎。為子弟者，能知此而順適其意，則盡其歡矣。 — The elderly act like infants; they delight in small monetary gains, in receiving small favors of food and fruit, and in playing intimately with children. If sons and younger brothers understand this and go along with their wishes, they will give them full happiness.

items.text: Serve your parents with sincere devotion; do not merely put on an outward show of respect.
items.quote: 人之孝行，根於誠篤，雖繁文末節不至，亦可以動天地、感鬼神。嘗見世人有事親不務誠篤，乃以聲音笑貌繆為恭敬者。 — Filial conduct is rooted in sincerity; even if elaborate rites and minor points are not fully performed, it can move heaven and earth and move the spirits. I have seen people who in serving parents do not strive for sincerity but pretend respect with voice and smile.

items.text: Give your children a proper occupation; idle rich sons fall into vice.
items.quote: 人之有子，須使有業。貧賤而有業，則不至於饑寒；富貴而有業，則不至於為非。 — If you have sons, you must see that they have an occupation; if poor and lowly but with an occupation, they will not starve or freeze; if rich and noble but with an occupation, they will not do evil.
